title: Four Victims of Ukhrul Ambush Brought to Imphal; Tangkhul Naga Long Issues Three-Day Ultimatum
summary: Four Tangkhul Naga civilians killed in the November 13 Ukhrul ambush were brought to Imphal as the Tangkhul Naga Long issued a three-day ultimatum demanding an NIA probe and security action.
body:
IMPHAL: The bodies of four Tangkhul Naga civilians killed in an ambush along National Highway 202 in Manipur’s Ukhrul district were brought to Imphal on November 14, following the deadly attack near New Haven on November 13. The incident has triggered strong condemnation from Tangkhul Naga organisations, with the Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL) issuing a three-day ultimatum to the Central and Manipur governments.

According to reports, unidentified armed men opened fire on two vehicles travelling towards Imphal along the Imphal–Ukhrul road at around 1 pm on Friday. The attack took place near New Haven under Litan Police Station, killing all four occupants.

The victims were identified as Kapangkhui RS and Haoleila RS from Shangshak Khullen village, and Tychicus Ngalung and Tanmila Keishing from Tashar village. The two victims from Shangshak were siblings, while those from Tashar were a mother and her son.

The Tangkhul Naga Long condemned the attack and described it as a serious failure of the security arrangements in the area. The organisation claimed that the incident occurred close to a security force deployment point and alleged that it was the fourth such attack at the same location.

**Tangkhul Naga Long Sets Three-Day Deadline**

Following an emergency meeting with Tangkhul civil society organisations, the TNL issued a three-day ultimatum to the Government of India and the Government of Manipur, demanding immediate action over the killings.

Among its key demands, the organisation called for the case to be handed over to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for investigation and demanded the removal of alleged armed Kuki militants from Naga-inhabited areas. It also expressed a loss of confidence in the central security forces deployed in the area and called for their withdrawal.

The organisation warned that failure to address its demands within the stipulated three days would lead to an indefinite public agitation. The deadline, following the November 13 statement, falls on November 16.

**Families Withhold Claim to Bodies**

The TNL also stated that the families of the four deceased civilians had decided not to claim the bodies until the organisation’s demands were addressed.

The decision has added to the urgency of the demands for an investigation and accountability. The organisation has called upon the authorities to take concrete steps to address the security concerns raised by the community.

**Security Operations Underway**

Following the ambush, additional security personnel from Manipur Police, the Border Security Force, the Army and Assam Rifles were deployed in the affected area. Search operations were also launched to trace those involved in the attack, according to police information reported by India Today NE.

The killings have heightened tensions in the region amid recent incidents of violence involving civilians in Ukhrul and neighbouring districts. The identity and responsibility of the attackers remain subject to investigation, and the allegations raised by community organisations have not yet been established through a formal probe.

The three-day ultimatum now places pressure on the State and Central governments to respond to the demands, while security agencies continue efforts to identify those responsible for the ambush.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
